deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the prime-number paper. It is the start of a different letter, or a draft continuation of the letter on the previous page. That letter accompanied the 1859 prime-number memoir and was almost certainly addressed to Weierstrass. The present text is the draft of what was published posthumously as 'Auszug aus einem Schreiben Riemann's an Weierstrass', J. reine angew. Math. 71 (1870), reprinted in Riemann's Werke. Its subject is the proof that a single-valued (einwerthige) function of n complex variables cannot have more than 2n independent periods. Riemann says he gave the proof in his lecture course of Winter 1855/56. He says he stated it unclearly in a recent conversation with the addressee, so he writes it out here.

Setup (modern notation):
- f : C^n -> C is single-valued.
- f has 2n period vectors a_mu = (a_mu^1, ..., a_mu^n) in C^n, mu = 1..2n. So f(x + a_mu) = f(x), where a_mu^nu is the 'Periodicitätsmodul' of x_nu for the mu-th period.
- Implicit assumption (mine): the 2n vectors a_mu, viewed in C^n = R^{2n}, are linearly independent over R.

Step 1 ('bekanntlich'). Under that assumption, every x in C^n can be written uniquely as x_nu = sum_{mu=1}^{2n} a_mu^nu xi_mu with xi_mu real. This is just solving a real 2n x 2n linear system: separate the real and imaginary parts of the n complex equations.

Step 2. Let each xi_mu run over [0,1), one endpoint excluded. This gives the half-open fundamental parallelotope P = { sum xi_mu a_mu : 0 <= xi_mu < 1 }. Every point x is congruent, modulo the lattice Lambda = Z a_1 + ... + Z a_{2n} (the '2n Modulsysteme'), to exactly one point of P. Explicitly (mine): replace each xi_mu by its fractional part xi_mu - floor(xi_mu). Riemann names P 'das bei diesen 2n Modulsystemen periodisch sich wiederholende Grössengebiet'. In modern terms it is a fundamental domain of the lattice, and P is a set of representatives of the real torus C^n / Lambda.

Step 3 (page breaks off). 'Hat die Function nun noch ein 2n+1tes Modulsystem ...' The argument is completed in the published letter, not on this page. Write the extra period as b = sum beta_mu a_mu with real beta_mu. Reduce the multiples k*b modulo Lambda into P. By the pigeonhole principle (Dirichlet), two of the reduced points come arbitrarily close. Hence f has arbitrarily small non-zero periods, unless b lies in Lambda, i.e. unless it is not really a new period. A limiting argument then shows that f is constant along some real direction. By analyticity and single-valuedness this leads to the conclusion that f effectively depends on fewer variables, or is constant. Hence a genuine (non-degenerate) function cannot have more than 2n independent periods.
errors: No mathematical error on the page.

The word 'bekanntlich' hides a hypothesis. The real decomposition x = sum a_mu xi_mu exists for all x, and is unique, only if the 2n period vectors are R-linearly independent in R^{2n}. Riemann does not state this explicitly here.
With 'mit Ausschluss eines von diesen Grenzwerthen' the exclusion must be the same endpoint for each coordinate, e.g. [0,1) throughout, for the uniqueness claim to hold exactly. This is implicit.

results.what: Representation of points of C^n in real coordinates with respect to 2n R-independent period vectors, and the half-open fundamental parallelotope giving unique representatives modulo the period lattice.
results.modern_name: Fundamental domain (period parallelotope) of a lattice in C^n = R^{2n}; real torus C^n/Lambda
results.usually_credited_to: Standard; implicit in Jacobi and Riemann on abelian functions (1850s)

results.what: Theorem announced here, with the proof begun: a single-valued function of n complex variables cannot have more than 2n independent periods.
results.modern_name: Riemann–Weierstrass theorem on the maximum number of periods (generalization of Jacobi's theorem that a single-valued function of one variable cannot be triply periodic)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (n=1, 1835); Riemann (letter to Weierstrass 1859, publ. Crelle 71, 1870); Weierstrass

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Riemann's known letter to Weierstrass. It was published in Crelle 71 (1870) and appears in the Werke, so the result is already credited to him. The only minor novelties are the draft wording and its placement next to the cover letter for the prime-number memoir. The 1855/56 lecture date is already stated in the published letter.

checkable.sympy: xi1, xi2 = symbols('xi1 xi2', real=True); solve([re(expand((1+0*I)*xi1 + (Rational(1,2)+I*sqrt(3)/2)*xi2 - (Rational(7,3)+I*Rational(5,4)))), im(expand((1+0*I)*xi1 + (Rational(1,2)+I*sqrt(3)/2)*xi2 - (Rational(7,3)+I*Rational(5,4))))], [xi1, xi2])
checkable.asserts: For n=1 with R-independent periods 1 and e^{i*pi/3}, an arbitrary complex x has a unique real coordinate pair (xi1, xi2).
The real 2x2 period matrix (columns are the periods as real vectors) is non-singular. This is the condition behind 'bekanntlich'.
Reduction of a coordinate into [0,1) differs from it by an integer. This is the uniqueness of the representative in the half-open fundamental domain.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'eindeutige' should probably read 'einwerthige', matching the published title of the letter ('einwerthige mehr als 2n fach periodische Function'). The image fits 'einwerthige'.
The transcription is otherwise essentially correct. The page is the start of the letter on periodic functions of several variables, not part of the prime-number text.
